skill.name: doc-coauthoring
skill.description: Guide users through a structured workflow for co-authoring documentation. Use when user wants to write documentation, proposals, technical specs, decision docs, or similar structured content. This workflow helps users efficiently transfer context, refine content through iteration, and verify the doc works for readers. Trigger when user mentions writing docs, creating proposals, drafting specs, or similar documentation tasks.
skill.summary: Guide users through context gathering, section drafting, refinement, and reader testing for stronger documents.
skill.author: anthropics

content.user_title: Draft Stronger Documents With Guided Coauthoring
content.value_statement: Complex documents often fail because context stays implicit or structure arrives too late. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through gathering context, drafting sections, refining edits, and testing reader understanding.
actual_capabilities: Runs a three-stage workflow for context gathering, section refinement, and reader testing.
Asks targeted questions about audience, goals, templates, constraints, and missing context.
Builds document structure with section placeholders before drafting detailed content.
Guides iterative section edits using specific feedback instead of full document rewrites.
Suggests reader testing questions and checks for ambiguity, assumptions, and contradictions.
Adapts to available artifacts, local files, integrations, or manual testing workflows.
limitations: It does not verify factual accuracy without user review or reliable source material.
It cannot access team channels or shared documents unless approved integrations are available.
It depends on the user to provide organizational context and final ownership decisions.
Reader testing may be manual when sub-agents or fresh model sessions are unavailable.

use_cases.title: Write a Technical Spec
use_cases.description: Turn architecture notes and constraints into a structured technical specification with clear trade-offs.

use_cases.title: Draft a Decision Document
use_cases.description: Capture decision context, alternatives, risks, and expected impact for stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Proposal
use_cases.description: Develop a proposal section by section and test whether readers understand the recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Document
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a guided document workflow from a rough idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me coauthor a document about [topic]. Ask me the initial context questions, then guide me through structure and drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Existing Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert notes into a workable document outline.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have rough notes for a [document type]. Help me identify the audience, goal, structure, and first section to draft.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Difficult Section
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve one section through questions, options, and focused edits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me improve the [section name] section. Ask clarifying questions, brainstorm possible points, then draft a focused revision.

prompt_templates.title: Test Reader Understanding
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate whether a finished draft works for new readers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Test this document as a new reader. Predict likely reader questions, identify ambiguity, and suggest specific fixes for weak sections.

output_examples.input: I need a decision doc for replacing our deployment process.
output_examples.output: The skill asks about audience, desired impact, current process, constraints, and alternatives. It then proposes sections such as context, options, decision, risks, rollout, and open questions.

output_examples.input: Here are notes for a technical spec, but the approach section is unclear.
output_examples.output: The skill asks targeted questions, brainstorms points to include, helps select the strongest ideas, and drafts a clearer approach section.

output_examples.input: Review this proposal before I share it with leadership.
output_examples.output: The skill predicts reader questions, checks for missing assumptions, highlights ambiguity, and recommends focused revisions before publication.

best_practices: Provide audience, goals, constraints, templates, and relevant background before asking for polished prose.
Work section by section so feedback can improve later sections.
Use reader testing before sharing important documents with real stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Do not skip context gathering when the topic has hidden organizational or technical history.
Do not ask for a full rewrite when focused section edits would preserve useful structure.
Do not treat reader testing as fact checking for claims that need source verification.

faq.question: What types of documents does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports technical specs, proposals, decision documents, RFCs, PRDs, and similar structured writing tasks.

faq.question: Can it use existing templates?
faq.answer: Yes. Share the template or describe it, and the workflow can build the draft around that structure.

faq.question: Does it write the full document at once?
faq.answer: No. It prefers section-by-section drafting so each part can reflect user feedback and context.

faq.question: Can it read shared documents or team channels?
faq.answer: Only when approved integrations or connectors are available. Otherwise, paste the relevant context directly.

faq.question: What is reader testing?
faq.answer: Reader testing checks whether a fresh reader can understand the document, answer likely questions, and spot ambiguity.

faq.question: Who is responsible for final quality?
faq.answer: The user remains responsible for final review, factual accuracy, links, and decisions before sharing the document.
